label: Executable OpenCode plugins have no Vibe equivalent: Vibe imports only portable skills and declarative MCP servers from an OpenCode package and never evaluates executables or custom tools.
Vibe declares seven hook types with strict blocking only for pre_tool, post_tool and pre_agent, declared in .vibe/hooks.toml or ~/.vibe/hooks.toml.
The spec gate ports partially: a strict pre_tool hook can block a tool call, but it needs a hook script, a TOML declaration and a payload adapter.
Dispatch preflight hooks port partially through pre_tool and pre_agent, with per-dispatch state moved under .vibe/ or the packet.
The session-relaunch loop has no equivalent: Vibe exposes no idle, compaction or resume hook, so a port needs an external supervisor reading export.json outcomes.
Goal and context bridges are partial: AGENTS.md and .vibe/prompts cover context injection, but there is no goal-state surface.
Slash commands have no equivalent: no .vibe/commands discovery exists, and .vibe/prompts is a prompt-template directory resolved by prompt id, not a user command catalogue with $ARGUMENTS.
Custom agents are a partial match: Vibe TOML profiles carry display_name, description, safety, agent_type, instructions and overrides, so markdown+YAML agents need a renderer.

Skills are equivalent: the same YAML-frontmatter markdown format parsed by parse_skill_markdown, discovered from skill_paths, .vibe/skills and .agents/skills, so pointing skill_paths at .skilled/skills is the cheapest port.
MCP is equivalent through stdio/HTTP server config with static auth or OAuth; the repository's MCP routing plugin has no analogue but the server contract ports by config.
MCP Code Mode has no equivalent: the builtin tool set (bash, edit, grep, read_file, write_file, skill, task, todo, web_fetch, web_search, ask_user_question) contains no script or execute tool.
Permissions have a partial equivalent through per-tool settings and approval agents with SAFE/NEUTRAL/DESTRUCTIVE/SMART/YOLO safety, while the self-invocation guard would be a strict pre_tool hook.
